video_title: THORChain Refused to Block the $387M Bitget Hacker. Here’s Why | Chad Barraford
gist: THORChain technical lead Chad Barraford defends why the protocol refused to block the $387M Bitget hacker, arguing it structurally cannot censor (no admin key, slow consensus) and that decentralization means 'I can't' rather than 'I won't'. Also covers the May GG20 exploit and 39-day halt, Tether's brief vault freeze, Monero/Zcash listings and a DEX-vs-CEX thesis.

themes.theme: Can't vs won't: decentralization as censorship resistance

insights.claim: THORChain's technical lead argues a protocol is only as decentralized as its most centralized component, so any chain where an individual or small group can pause trades (e.g. Near Intents, Chainflip) is not truly DeFi.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Gives a usable screen for which cross-chain swap venues carry hidden admin or censorship risk.
insights.quote: you're only as decentralized as your most centralized component

insights.claim: THORChain was deliberately designed so that no admin key exists and validators cannot talk privately, so the team cannot block wallets or trades even if it wanted to; consensus to halt a specific transaction would take roughly 3 days to 2 weeks, by which time funds have already swapped out.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Structural inability to censor makes THORChain a durable exit route for hackers, which is a permanent reputational and legal overhang on RUNE.

insights.claim: Barraford says any chain, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, could block stolen funds if a majority agreed, but Bitcoin would need only about three mining pools for 51% whereas THORChain would need a larger number of independent operators (about 110-115 validators run by roughly 50 operators).
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Counters the claim that THORChain is uniquely easy to coordinate; the censorship debate is about willingness, not capability.

insights.claim: Mechanisms to freeze individual wallets would require every operator to buy a chain-analytics subscription (TRM or Chainalysis) costing about $250,000 a year, adding millions to network operating costs.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: A concrete cost barrier showing why compliance retrofits on permissionless validators are economically unattractive.

insights.claim: Pausing a specific asset pool after a hack has no workable resume condition, since you could never know when malicious actors would stop using the protocol, so a pause would effectively shut the protocol down permanently.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Explains why THORChain treats pool-level freezes as an existential, not operational, risk.

insights.claim: After the roughly $387.5M Bitget hack, Bitget CEO Gracie Chen publicly asked THORChain to refuse service to the attacker addresses, and THORChain declined; Barraford says the official ask was just a tweet with no direct contact with validators or operators.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Shows a large-exchange hack can flow through a DEX with no coordinated response channel, raising odds of future regulatory pressure on such venues.

insights.claim: There is little appetite among THORChain validators to block individual wallets or transactions; during the earlier Bybit hack (about $1.4B) a faction of roughly 10-20% of validators wanted to stop and lost by a landslide, and around 20 validators left, yet the validator count today exceeds what it was then.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Evidence the network self-selects for non-censoring operators and has grown despite earlier public controversies.

insights.claim: Hackers want to exit crypto into dollars, and Bitcoin is the easiest bridge because it is the most liquid asset with the most on- and off-ramps, so THORChain's native swaps to BTC and ETH make it a natural route for laundering regardless of intent.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Implies the real chokepoints are the centralized off-ramps, where enforcement is more likely to be targeted.
insights.quote: The goal is to get out of crypto entirely into dollars.

insights.claim: Barraford argues enforcement should target the centralized exchanges that knowingly accept illicit Bitcoin (for example, for a higher fee, accepting fake passports) rather than the on-chain swap protocol.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Signals where he expects, and wants, regulators to aim; a risk to off-ramp venues more than to THORChain.

insights.claim: Barraford estimates stolen funds are about 1% and no more than 2% of THORChain's roughly $125-127B cumulative trade volume, and compares the fee income from hacks to Bitcoin miners earning fees on any transaction.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Rebuts the claim that THORChain's revenue depends on hack flows, though the figure is an unaudited guess (he says he did not run a formal analysis).

insights.claim: Barraford says the halting precedent differs: THORChain validators will quickly halt trading to protect the protocol itself (three nodes can vote to halt), but will not halt for an external party's hack because validators owe no duty to outside entities like Bitget.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Distinction between protecting protocol security and policing third-party theft is the core of THORChain's defense and likely of future disputes.

themes.theme: May exploit and GG20 cryptography risk

insights.claim: In May, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in THORChain's GG20 threshold-signature implementation to extract other participants' key shares and drain one of six vaults of about $10.7M.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Shows threshold-signature vault custody remains an exploitable single class of risk for cross-chain protocols.

insights.claim: THORChain trading halted for about 39 days after the exploit because lack of logs meant the team had to find and verify the exact root cause (it found more than one issue), and the team made the GG20 library closed source temporarily and plans to migrate to FROST or DKLS.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: A month-plus outage and a planned cryptography migration are execution risks and a possible catalyst for RUNE sentiment on relaunch and open-sourcing.

insights.claim: THORChain validators follow the dev team's recommendation to halt when the protocol is at risk, but the team cannot coordinate privately with validators as Bitcoin and Ethereum developers can with miners to quietly roll out security patches.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: The anonymity-by-design that protects against censorship also slows security response, a tradeoff for protocol risk assessment.

themes.theme: Tether freeze of THORChain vaults and stablecoin risk

insights.claim: Earlier this month Tether blacklisted four THORChain vaults (about $1.4M of Tron USDT) without notice and reversed it hours later; Barraford believes it was a mistake from a hack response where Tether treated protocol addresses as ordinary wallets.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Shows that DeFi vaults holding centralized stablecoins can be frozen by error, a live counterparty risk.

insights.claim: Barraford argues a centralized stablecoin issuer that froze DeFi protocol vaults would be committing suicide, since LPs and holders would withdraw from every protocol and swap into competitors.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Market discipline is the claimed protection, but it is untested against a deliberate, regulator-driven freeze.

insights.claim: Chainflip uses USDC as the base asset for all its pools, so a Circle freeze of its vaults would end the protocol, whereas THORChain's USDT exposure is a small share of TVL and could simply be delisted.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Competitor fragility claim: protocols with a centralized stablecoin base pair carry existential issuer risk.

themes.theme: Privacy coins: Zcash, Monero and demand

insights.claim: THORChain added Zcash a couple of weeks ago (transparent addresses only, with no unusual volume seen) and is working to add Monero soon, which Barraford calls technically extremely difficult and expects to be the first Monero integration of its kind.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Monero listing is a possible volume and fee catalyst for THORChain and a new regulatory flashpoint.

insights.claim: Barraford expects THORChain could become the largest Monero exchange in the world, the first time a DEX is the primary market for a top-10 coin, because most centralized exchanges do not support Monero and holders want to avoid KYC.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Concentrated Monero liquidity on a permissionless venue raises the delisting and enforcement risk for the protocol, as well as the upside for RUNE fees.

insights.claim: Barraford says THORChain does no mixing or obfuscation, even for Monero, so all flow data is publicly visible in real time and regulators need no subpoena; his own conversations with agencies were non-adversarial and ended after they concluded he has little or no control over the protocol.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Suggests regulators have so far accepted the control-based test of decentralization, but this rests on one operator's account.

themes.theme: Strategy: long-tail chains, AI, and DEX vs CEX

insights.claim: THORChain is shifting from supporting only major assets to adding many more chains (Tao and Substrate, Dash, Zeno, UTXO-style chains, Bitcoin Cash subtokens) so integrators like wallets do not need a second swap through another DEX.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: Broader asset coverage can raise the share of swap flow THORChain captures and compete directly with aggregators.
insights.quote: I think historically we were thinking about being more on the short side of the PTO curve

insights.claim: Barraford says AI has cut the cost of adding technically complex chains, and that THORChain would not be adding Monero now without it.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: AI-assisted integration lowers the engineering moat and lets small crypto teams expand coverage faster.
insights.quote: I don't think we would be adding Monero right now if AI did not exist

insights.claim: Barraford predicts DEXs will beat centralized exchanges on swaps over the next 5-10 years because they offer instant liquidity, no KYC, one-click trades and lower cost, with the main obstacle being institutional hesitancy from regulatory uncertainty that he expects to fade.
insights.speaker: Chad Barraford (THORChain technical lead)
insights.so_what: A stated bullish industry view from an interested party; the regulatory convergence is the key assumption to watch.
